rulings.raw: 1.75 - 2.5 kg / 3.5 - 5lb pork loin OR shoulder/boston butt ( ,or scotch fillet, skinless (Note 1))
rulings.evidence: REUSE, not a new id: pork-loin is live on the everyday board (Member's Mark whole boneless pork loin, priced per lb, plus Kroger cells). Loin is the title's first option and the macro check settles it - loin gives 55 g protein/serving against the source's 56, while pork-shoulder gives 46 g and 738 cal.
Composite line booked on the larger food: 2 tsp paprika at 2.4 g/tsp. The 2 tsp of thyme in a dry rub is DRIED thyme (not the fresh-thyme id) and rides the buy string uncosted at about 2 g.

rulings.raw: 1 tsp EACH garlic powder, onion powder
rulings.evidence: Composite line booked on garlic powder (1 tsp = 3.1 g, existing macro row); the matching 1 tsp onion powder (2.4 g) rides the buy string. Both foods already exist, neither is a new id.
Black Pepper is an exact vocabulary row and the bell-pepper near-misses are a token artifact; unqualified 'pepper' in a spice rub is ground black pepper. 2.3 g/tsp label basis.

Cider vinegar IS apple cider vinegar. REUSE: apple-cider-vinegar is a live commodity with captured cells (Great Value, Kroger, Bragg) on the everyday board. NOT apple-cider, which is the drink - form flip.
1/2 tsp each: salt booked at 3 g (matching the settled 2 tsp = 12 g basis), the matching 1/2 tsp black pepper rides the buy string. Sauce seasoning, distinct from the rub salt line.

rulings.raw: 3 tsp cornflour/cornstarch mixed with splash of water
rulings.evidence: Cornflour is the British name for the same food; exact vocabulary row and a 7 of 7 board id. Not wheat flour, which the word means in no US context here.

macro_cross_check.verdict: PASS - the closest match in the batch. Protein within 2% and carbohydrate within 1.4% both confirm the two judgement calls: the cut is LEAN LOIN (shoulder would land at 46 g protein and 738 cal) and the 2125 g midpoint of the source's own 1.75-2.5 kg range is right. The carbohydrate agreement also proves the source counts the WHOLE honey butter sauce, not a served fraction, which is why calories run 8% high rather than the sauce being over-booked. In band on both run conditions (606 cal, 27.6 g carb).
